doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Melody in Dixieland brass music versus rock and roll
summary: The men prefer playing a melody people can follow; one keeps a rock instrument only just in case.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, I'll say this much, since I've been fooling with any kind of music, the Vixalayan jazz is the only music that you can really understand and give your most spirit to dance and everything else that I haven't seen myself. Well, that's what you do. Of course, I'm not down in the ground. You call it when you play. When you play, you see. Like that. You got a bad melody. But ever since I've been a man, and before I know how to play any kind of music, I heard Vixalayan brass band play and everything else. And I said to myself, that's a wonderful music that they were playing. I said that to myself. They didn't know anything about it.

And long ago, long ago, you know what I was playing? People want to play now what they can sing, what they understand. Would you play a melody? You ain't no way. You see, you take a- And then? That's right. That's right. That melody, if you don't listen, I don't want to dispute the band where they're playing now, them rock and roll band. I can play a tough too, but I want some melody where I can follow. I want to play a melody. Let you understand you, your family. Jim Robinson playing a melody on a trombone. I want to sing it to you. What I'm making there?
You know where you're humming that? I had a dream.

So far as the rock and roll. I keep instrument to play rock and roll in case if somebody jumped me up. I keep that kind of instrument to play rock and roll. But see like this, this ain't no rock and roll instrument.
